title: Long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen plasma control samples for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and human immunodeficiency virus by quantitative PCR: Implications for retrospective testing in hemovigilance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen virus-positive samples in quantitative PCR assays to provide evidence for their analytical reliability in retrospective NAT and quality assurance, addressing the limited data on this topic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the long-term performance of frozen virus-positive samples in quantitative PCR assays over 37 months for HIV, 25 and 29 months for HBV-A and HBV-B, and 49 and 38 months for HCV-A and HCV-B, using internal run controls from positive patient samples.
analysis.methods: The study used diluted and aliquoted internal run controls from positive patient samples, analyzed using routine quantitative PCR assays, and assessed variability and temporal trends using descriptive statistics and linear regression.
analysis.main_results: All internal run controls demonstrated stable long-term performance during frozen storage and routine use, with 99.2%–100% of measurements remaining within the acceptance range, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support the suitability of long-term stored specimens for retrospective NAT, providing robust evidence for the long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen HBV-, HCV-, and HIV-positive samples in routine quantitative PCR assays.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings are relevant for look-back investigations in hemovigilance and support the use of long-term stored specimens for retrospective NAT, enhancing the safety of blood transfusions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the evaluation of only internal run controls and the potential lack of generalizability to other types of samples or assays, but the evidence is strong due to the robust performance of the controls within the acceptance range.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen virus-positive samples in quantitative PCR assays, demonstrating that these samples remain analytically reliable for up to 4 years, supporting their use in retrospective NAT and enhancing hemovigilance.

title: Associated factors of hepatitis B virus infection among pregnant women in Africa: an extension of a previous systematic review and meta-analysis on prevalence

analysis.scope_and_question: We assessed methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted separate random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian–Laird method for each associated factor reported by at least two studies to estimate pooled adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Associated factors examined across multiple studies that differed substantially in exposure categories or reference groups were synthesized narratively.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: While previous reviews have focused on the prevalence of HBV, comprehensive evidence regarding the associated factors of HBV infection is limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening, targeted risk assessment, vaccination strategies, and linkage-to-care interventions may help improve early detection and reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV.

analysis.summary_en: We assessed methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). We conducted separate random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian–Laird method for each associated factor reported by at least two studies to estimate pooled adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associated factors examined across multiple studies that differed substantially in exposure categories or reference groups were synthesized narratively. While previous reviews have focused on the prevalence of HBV, comprehensive evidence regarding the associated factors of HBV infection is limited. Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening, targeted risk assessment, vaccination strategies, and linkage-to-care interventions may help improve early detection and reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV.

title: Hepatitis B Virus Knowledge, Preventive Practices, and Vaccination Status Among People Living with HIV at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research, Lagos: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.scope_and_question: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) co-infection substantially increases liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLHIV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0, through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression with statistical significance set at p<0.05.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV.

analysis.summary_en: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) co-infection substantially increases liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLHIV). Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0, through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression with statistical significance set at p<0.05. Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010). The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes. This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response to antiviral therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not all.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the potential of machine learning to improve prediction of fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the application of ML in clinical and pathological data integration, and dynamic treatment response prediction.
analysis.methods: The authors review how machine learning can be applied to analyze medical images, integrate clinical and pathological data, and predict treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: The authors highlight early but encouraging results from three areas: quantitative image analysis using ML, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning's greatest value lies in complementing existing tools, particularly for identifying patients unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone, rather than replacing them.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that machine learning could enhance the precision of predicting treatment outcomes in chronic hepatitis B, aiding in personalized approaches to therapy and improving patient management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The authors note that current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which limits their generalizability and requires prospective multi-center validation for clinical adoption.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of machine learning to improve the prediction of liver fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B patients. It highlights the limitations of conventional clinical tools and emphasizes the need for more robust, personalized approaches. The authors suggest that ML can complement existing methods by identifying patients who may not benefit from antiviral therapy alone, but they caution that current models require validation in larger, multi-center studies to ensure their reliability and applicability in clinical settings.

title: Point of Care Diagnostics for Hepatitis B and C in Low-resource Settings: A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of Point-Of-Care (POC) diagnostics in improving the detection and management of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in low-resource settings. The central question is whether POC testing can enhance the accessibility and effectiveness of HBV diagnosis, particularly in regions with limited laboratory infrastructure.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and grey literature. It assesses the state of POC technologies, their diagnostic performance, and implementation challenges in resource-limited settings. The review does not report specific eligibility criteria, study counts, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: POC diagnostics have the potential to accelerate hepatitis elimination by improving access to rapid testing. Their successful implementation requires strengthened health systems, trained healthcare workers, and integration into existing healthcare services. New technologies, such as mobile healthcare integration and AI-powered interpretation, enhance their capabilities.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are still areas of challenge, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, that make it difficult to scale POC diagnostics for HBV. The review highlights that existing challenges and future opportunities for improving access to timely and effective diagnosis remain underexplored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Improving access to timely and effective HBV diagnosis is crucial for clinical intervention and global elimination. The review emphasizes the need for addressing supply chain issues, policy adoption, and social stigma to scale POC diagnostics. It also suggests the importance of integrating new technologies into healthcare systems to enhance diagnostic capabilities.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review evaluates the potential of Point-Of-Care (POC) diagnostics to improve the detection and management of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in low-resource settings. It highlights the importance of timely diagnosis for clinical intervention and global elimination, noting that POC technologies can enhance accessibility and effectiveness. The review identifies key challenges, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, which hinder the scalability of POC diagnostics. It also discusses the integration of new technologies, such as mobile healthcare and AI-powered interpretation, to strengthen diagnostic capabilities. The review underscores the need for improved health systems, trained personnel, and policy support to fully realize the benefits of POC testing for HBV.

title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Approved chronic hepatitis B therapies rarely result in functional cure, as they fail to permanently silence all transcriptionally active hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA.
analysis.study_design_and_population: CRMA-1001 employs an optimized epigenetic silencer that represses viral transcription through targeted deposition of DNA methylation on episomal and integrated HBV DNAs.
analysis.methods: Here we showed that in HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 produced >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, which correlated with de novo methylation of HBV DNA.
analysis.main_results: Three doses resulted in up to 90% of animals with undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post treatment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In non-human primates, CRMA-1001 induced transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Expression and DNA methylation profiling revealed no detectable unintended targets in the human genome.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings support the initiation of clinical development of CRMA-1001 as a finite treatment course with the potential for functional cure in individuals living with chronic hepatitis B.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the limitations of current hepatitis B virus (HBV) therapies, which rarely achieve a functional cure by failing to silence all transcriptionally active HBV DNA. The research focused on CRMA-1001, an epigenetic silencer designed to repress viral transcription through DNA methylation. In HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 led to >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, with three doses achieving up to 90% undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post-treatment. In non-human primates, the therapy caused transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested, and no unintended targets were detected in the human genome. These results suggest that CRMA-1001 could be a promising finite treatment for chronic HBV, potentially leading to a functional cure. However, the study's findings are based on animal models, and further clinical trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety in humans.

title: Molecular Evolution of Hepatitis B Virus in India: Insights into Genotype Diversity and Recombination

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major public health problem in India, with considerable genetic variability arising out of evolutionary selection pressure, recombination events and reverse-transcription stage in its life cycle.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Residual HBsAg positive samples (n = 1963), received for inter-laboratory quality control or for referral diagnostic testing between 2006 and 2023 were screened, and n = 172 of these were positive for HBV DNA by realtime PCR.
analysis.methods: HBV DNA positive samples with high viral load (n = 32), collected from nine states of India, were used for whole-genome sequencing. DNA extracted these serum samples was subjected to whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on the Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) MinION platform. Genotype-specific tiled amplicons (~ 1000 bp) were used for library preparation.
analysis.main_results: HBV genotype D (70.96%) was found to be common genotype in several Indian states, with genotype A (3.22%) present in central and southern states and genotype C (6.45%) in the northeast. Notably, five samples showed evidence of recombination events, including genotypes A, C, and D. SimPlot analysis of representative isolates showed clearly demarcated recombination breakpoints.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The present study emphasizes the genetic heterogeneity and evolutionary dynamics of HBV in India, and recombination as a key mechanism adding to viral diversity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The success in utilizing ONT for WGS of HBV directly from serum samples illustrates its utility for scalable genomic surveillance. The initiation of a nationwide HBV sequencing program will be pivotal in tracking emerging variants, informing therapeutic interventions, and facilitating India's role in the global HBV elimination drive.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular evolution of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in India, focusing on genotype diversity and recombination. The research highlights the genetic variability of HBV due to evolutionary pressures and recombination events, which influence transmission patterns, disease chronicity, and treatment response. Whole-genome sequencing of 32 HBV DNA positive samples from nine Indian states revealed genotype D as the most prevalent, followed by A and C. Five samples showed evidence of recombination, with clearly demarcated breakpoints identified through SimPlot analysis. The study underscores the importance of genomic surveillance in tracking HBV variants and informing public health strategies. The use of Oxford Nanopore Technology for direct sequencing from serum samples demonstrates its potential for scalable monitoring. The findings emphasize the need for a nationwide HBV sequencing program to support global elimination efforts.

title: Determinants of Adult Hepatitis B Vaccine Uptake in a High-Endemic Setting

analysis.research_question_and_background: Adult hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination remains a critical yet underutilized component of viral hepatitis prevention in many high-endemic settings. Although infant HBV vaccination has been widely integrated into national immunization programmes, adult vaccination often depends on individual awareness, healthcare access, and provider recommendation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a community-based cross-sectional survey among adults in Minna, Nigeria, using multistage sampling. Community-based evidence on the determinants of adult HBV vaccine uptake is needed to inform adult immunization strategies in resource-constrained settings.
analysis.methods: Data on sociodemographic characteristics, HBV-related knowledge, healthcare access, and vaccination status were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify factors independently associated with vaccine uptake, with adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported.
analysis.main_results: Among 426 participants, 167 (39.2%) had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the vaccination series. In bivariate analyses, vaccine uptake was significantly associated with education, occupation, residence type, ward, religion, HBV knowledge, and health worker recommendation (all p.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of sociodemographic and health-system factors in influencing adult HBV vaccine uptake, providing actionable insights for improving immunization strategies in high-endemic regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to improve adult HBV vaccination rates, particularly in resource-constrained settings where health worker recommendations and awareness play a pivotal role in vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and by potential biases related to self-reported data. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the determinants of adult hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine uptake in a high-endemic setting in Minna, Nigeria. It highlights the underutilization of adult HBV vaccination despite its importance in viral hepatitis prevention. The research focuses on individual and health-system level factors, such as education, occupation, healthcare access, and provider recommendations, which were found to significantly influence vaccine uptake. The study employs a community-based cross-sectional survey with multistage sampling and uses modified Poisson regression to analyze associations. Among 426 participants, 39.2% had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the series. The findings suggest that improving health worker recommendations and increasing awareness could enhance adult vaccination rates. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to potential biases and the reliance on self-reported data.

title: Intradermal hepatitis B vaccination with or without Imiquimod in cirrhosis after prior vaccine nonresponse: A Randomised Trial.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Patients with cirrhosis show impaired immune responses to standard intramuscular (IM) hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, resulting in low seroconversion rates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a randomized controlled pilot trial to compare three HBV revaccination strategies in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) who previously failed standard IM vaccination: IM revaccination, ID revaccination, and ID revaccination combined with imiquimod (ID+IMQ).
analysis.methods: This monocentric, prospective study included 59 patients with ACLD and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL after prior HBV vaccination. Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive either IM vaccination (n=19; Engerix-B® 20 μg IM at Months 0, 1 and 6), ID vaccination (n=19; two 10 μg ID injections at the same time points), or ID vaccination preceded by topical imiquimod 5% application (n=21).
analysis.main_results: In the intention-to-treat analysis, seroprotection rates at month 7 were 36.8% in the IM group, 84.2% in the ID group, and 66.7% in the ID+IMQ group (p<0.01). After Bonferroni correction, only the ID versus IM comparison remained statistically significant (p=0.003). Geometric mean anti-HBs titres were significantly higher in the ID (116 mIU/mL) and ID+IMQ (107 mIU/mL) groups compared with the IM group (12 mIU/mL) (p=0.004).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Intradermal HBV revaccination significantly improves seroconversion in non-responder patients with ACLD compared with IM vaccination, without additional benefit from imiquimod.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support further evaluation of intradermal vaccination without imiquimod in a phase 3 trial.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intradermal (ID) hepatitis B vaccination, with or without imiquimod, in patients with cirrhosis who previously failed standard intramuscular (IM) vaccination. A randomized controlled pilot trial was conducted with 59 patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL. The primary endpoint was seroconversion at Month 7, defined as anti-HBs titres ≥10 mIU/mL. The results showed that seroprotection rates were significantly higher in the ID group (84.2%) compared to the IM group (36.8%), with no additional benefit from imiquimod. The study suggests that ID vaccination may be a more effective strategy for HBV revaccination in non-responder patients with ACLD, warranting further investigation in larger trials.

title: Effectiveness of Radio Messages in Reducing Public Hesitancy Toward Hepatitis B Vaccination in Selected North-Central States of Nigeria

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The central question is whether radio messages can improve awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance among the population, particularly in the context of misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a survey research design, collecting data through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states. Secondary data were obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that radio messages were ineffective in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination due to poor message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content. These factors limited knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. The findings suggest that radio as a health communication tool has significant limitations in the context of Hepatitis B vaccination in the North-Central states of Nigeria.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights the limitations of radio messages in addressing public hesitancy, but it does not provide comparative data with other communication strategies. There is no mention of how the effectiveness of radio messages might vary across different demographic groups or how other factors such as socioeconomic status or education level might influence vaccine acceptance. The evidence also lacks information on the long-term impact of radio messages on vaccination behavior.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear. It also suggests that radio stations and health authorities should address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The study found that radio messages were ineffective due to poor design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, which limited knowledge acquisition and trust building. The review highlights the need for careful evaluation and redesign of radio messages to ensure cultural relevance and clarity, as well as addressing infrastructural and audience-related challenges to improve vaccine uptake. The findings suggest that radio, while a potential health communication tool, requires strategic improvements to be effective in this context.

title: Genotypic variability and the mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus among HIV‐infected patients living in the regions of Western Siberia (Russia)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify and characterize the variants of hepatitis B virus in HIV-infected patients from three geographically close regions of Western Siberia (Novosibirsk Region, Tomsk Region, and the Altai Republic). Hepatitis B is a major public health problem due to its prevalence, complications, and genetic variability, which requires detailed molecular characterization for effective treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 708 blood serum samples collected from patients with confirmed HIV infection. The incidence of HBV genetic material in the study group was 8.5% (95% CI = 6.6–10.8). The work analyzed 60 full-genomic sequences of the identified HBV variants.
analysis.methods: For primary screening for HBV DNA, a commercial "AmpliSens HBV-FL" kit was used. For the selected positive samples, next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform was used to obtain full-genomic HBV nucleotide sequences, which were serotyped, genotyped, and analyzed for the presence of clinically significant mutations.
analysis.main_results: The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, and mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results highlight the importance of continuous molecular monitoring for the development of diagnostic strategies, improving the effectiveness of vaccination, and clinical management of HBV patients, especially among people living with HIV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective diagnostic strategies, vaccination programs, and clinical management approaches for HBV patients, particularly those co-infected with HIV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides moderate confidence due to the limited geographic scope and the focus on a specific population, but the results are supported by detailed molecular analysis of full-genomic sequences.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genotypic variability and mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) among HIV-infected patients in three regions of Western Siberia. The research aimed to characterize HBV variants in this population, as HBV genetic diversity is critical for effective treatment and management. A total of 708 blood serum samples were analyzed, with 8.5% testing positive for HBV. Of these, 60 full-genomic sequences were obtained and classified as genotype D. Mutations in the S gene, BCP, PreCore, Core, and X genes were detected in all sequences, with high prevalence in the Core and X genes. The study emphasizes the need for continuous molecular monitoring to improve diagnostic strategies and clinical care for HBV patients, especially those co-infected with HIV. While the findings are significant for understanding HBV dynamics in this specific population, the study's moderate confidence is due to its limited geographic scope and focus on a particular demographic group.

title: Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Regarding Hepatitis-B Virus Infection among Slum Population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus infection in a low-literacy urban population. The background highlights that HBV infection is a significant cause of mortality and morbidity in developing countries, with prevalence rates varying by country.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 2000 adult slum residents in Dhaka City, Bangladesh, from July 2006 to June 2007. The population was selected through simple random sampling from 4966 slum clusters in the city.
analysis.methods: Trained interviewers collected data using validated questionnaires. Blood samples were taken from each participant for HbsAg testing, and the ELISA method confirmed positive cases.
analysis.main_results: 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, but specific understanding was limited. Only 7.06% knew HBV could be caused by an infectious agent, and 53.99% were unaware of transmission modes. Additionally, 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in Dhaka City’s urban slums, despite residents showing interest in learning more and getting tested.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for improved education and healthcare access in these communities to address the poor knowledge and low vaccination rates related to HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the potential for recall bias. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive data on knowledge and risk factors but lacks longitudinal or causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among the slum population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh. It found that while 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, specific understanding of HBV causes and transmission modes was limited. Only 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine, and risk factors included low literacy, economic constraints, and limited access to healthcare. The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in these communities, emphasizing the need for improved education and healthcare access. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

title: Awareness and Preventive Practices of Hepatitis B Virus Infection Among Pregnant Women in Bangladesh

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the relationship between awareness and preventive practices of HBV infection among pregnant women in Bangladesh due to the global health challenge posed by HBV infection, particularly in pregnant women.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive correlational study was conducted at the 250-Bedded General Hospital in Kushtia, involving 112 pregnant women selected through convenience sampling.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.
analysis.main_results: The study found that 80.4% of participants demonstrated limited awareness regarding disease transmission, symptoms, screening procedures, and vaccination, and 75% reported insufficient engagement in preventive practices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight a substantial deficiency in both awareness and implementation of preventive behaviors among pregnant women in Bangladesh, suggesting the need for comprehensive health education programs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted health education programs to increase awareness and improve preventive behaviors among pregnant women in Bangladesh, thereby reducing the risk of vertical transmission of HBV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a convenience sample and the potential for socio-demographic variables to confound the results, which may limit the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined the awareness and preventive practices of HBV infection among pregnant women in Bangladesh, finding that 80.4% had limited awareness and 75% engaged insufficiently in preventive practices. The findings suggest the need for comprehensive health education programs.

title: Assessment of Knowledge and Awareness Regarding Transmission and Risk Factors of HBV, HCV, and HIV among Health Sciences Students in Universities of Taiz, Yemen

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 health sciences students across five universities in Taiz, Yemen from September 2025 to July 2026.
analysis.methods: Stratified sampling was used to select participants based on university, discipline, and academic year. Data were collected using a self-administered, structured questionnaire that assessed knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, vaccination status for HBV, and occupational exposure.
analysis.main_results: The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students having good knowledge. Students at the clinical stage had higher good knowledge rates compared to pre-clinical students (57.0% vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight a significant knowledge gap among health sciences students, particularly in pre-clinical stages, and suggest the need for targeted educational interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is critical for reducing occupational transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the knowledge and awareness of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen, regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 students across five universities from September 2025 to July 2026, using stratified sampling and a self-administered questionnaire. The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students demonstrating good knowledge. Clinical-stage students had higher good knowledge rates than pre-clinical students (57.0% vs. 34.0%, p < 0.05). The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting a significant knowledge gap, particularly among pre-clinical students, and emphasized the need for targeted educational interventions. The study's results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is essential for reducing occupational transmission risks. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Post-vaccination immunity to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel: predictive modeling, key predictors, and risk management

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel to determine prognostic criteria and risk management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed serological screening results of 1,380 employees from a multidisciplinary medical center for anti-HBsAg and HBsAg in 2024-2025, along with their vaccination history data.
analysis.methods: Laboratory tests were conducted using enzyme immunoassay with the reagent set “Vecto HBsAg-antibodies” from JSC “Vector-Best”. A binary logistic regression model was constructed to identify predictors of positive immune response.
analysis.main_results: In 81.8% of the employees, the concentration of anti-HBsAg was more than 10 mIU/ml. Increasing age by 1 year lowered the chances of a positive result by 1,052 times. An increase in the period since the last injection of the vaccine for each year reduced the chances of a positive result by 1,055 times. Administration of each additional dose of the vaccine increased the chances of a positive result by 2,036 times. The model had a sensitivity of 73.9% and specificity of 73.7%, with an overall diagnostic significance of 73.8%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating the need for further study on the feasibility of booster immunization for medical workers, considering a comprehensive assessment of humoral and cellular immunity to effectively manage biological risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted booster immunization strategies for medical personnel to enhance post-vaccination immunity and reduce the risk of hepatitis B virus exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on serological data and a binary logistic regression model, which may not fully capture the complexity of immune responses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel, focusing on predictive modeling and key predictors. It analyzed serological screening data from 1,380 employees over 2024-2025, using enzyme immunoassay to measure anti-HBsAg levels. The results showed that 81.8% of employees had antibody concentrations above 10 mIU/ml, with age, time since last vaccination, and number of doses significantly affecting the likelihood of a positive result. The model demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity, suggesting its potential utility in risk management. The authors concluded that further research on booster immunization, incorporating both humoral and cellular immunity assessments, is necessary to improve hepatitis B virus risk management strategies in medical settings.

title: Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 levels in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B: associations with EASL-based clinical phenotypes, histological inflammatory activity, and non-invasive fibrosis indices

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major global health issue, as ongoing viral replication can drive hepatic inflammation and immune dysregulation, increasing the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 in CHB patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. In total, 86 individuals were enrolled: 21 healthy controls and 65 treatment-naive CHB patients. CHB patients were categorized by HBV DNA level into ≤ 105 IU/mL (n = 33) and > 105 IU/mL (n = 32).
analysis.methods: Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were measured by ELISA, and laboratory-based inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices were calculated. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were used to assess associations; ROC analyses were descriptive and exploratory.
analysis.main_results: Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 differed significantly among study groups and were highest in patients with elevated viral loads (both p < 0.001). Viral load correlated strongly with CXCL-10 (r = 0.786) and CTLA-4 (r = 0.559), and CXCL-10 correlated strongly with CTLA-4 (r = 0.690; all p < 0.001). Both CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 correlated more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score (r = 0.519 and r = 0.509, respectively; p < 0.001) than with fibrosis stage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest a role for CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 as markers of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activity in CHB, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of non-invasive biomarkers for assessing inflammatory activity in CHB, potentially improving diagnostic and monitoring strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and moderate sample size, with liver biopsy data available for only 43 patients (66.2%). The evidence strength is moderate, as the ROC performance was moderate (AUC 0.78 for CXCL-10; 0.76 for CTLA-4).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 levels in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. The research aimed to understand the role of these biomarkers in reflecting immune and inflammatory responses in CHB. Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were found to differ significantly among study groups, with higher levels observed in patients with elevated viral loads. Both biomarkers correlated strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score, indicating their potential as markers of inflammatory activity. The study's findings suggest that CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 may serve as useful indicators of immune and inflammatory status in CHB, though further validation in larger, longitudinal cohorts is needed. The study's cross-sectional design and limited sample size, particularly for liver biopsy data, may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate, as the ROC performance was moderate for both biomarkers.

analysis.scope_and_question: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not clearly state controversies or evidence gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings enrich the knowledge about the natural history of chronic hepatitis B in the region and reaffirm the importance of viral suppression in disease control.

analysis.summary_en: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil. A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025. Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure. The supplied evidence does not clearly state controversies or evidence gaps. title: Depression and medication adherence among chronic hepatitis B patients receiving resilience-based care versus standard care during antiviral therapy: a retrospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the association between receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence among patients with chronic hepatitis B undergoing antiviral therapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted involving 200 patients diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B and treated at the hepatology clinic of our hospital between July 2022 and June 2025. The study compared 100 patients who voluntarily completed a structured 12-week resilience promotion program with standard care (observation group) to 100 patients who received standard care only (control group).
analysis.methods: Multivariable linear, logistic, and Poisson regression models were used to account for potential confounding by indication and baseline imbalances, with adjusted effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals reported. The observation group had fewer unplanned outpatient visits, and Poisson regression confirmed this finding with an adjusted rate ratio of 0.72 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.93).
analysis.main_results: At the 6-month follow-up, the observation group had lower depression scores (6.78 ± 3.45 vs. 10.23 ± 4.12), higher medication possession ratio (MPR) (0.92 ± 0.08 vs. 0.78 ± 0.15), and higher resilience scores (32.45 ± 5.67 vs. Virological response was more frequent in the observation group (85.0% vs. 70.0%; adjusted OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.48), as was ALT normalization (80.0% vs. 65.0%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10 to 3.67). SF-36 physical and mental component scores were also higher in the observation group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the resilience-focused program in addition to standard care was associated with lower depressive symptoms, better medication adherence, and more favorable virological and biochemical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B. This finding highlights the potential benefit of integrating resilience-based care into the management of chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that resilience-based care could improve mental health and treatment outcomes for patients with chronic hepatitis B, potentially informing future strategies for enhancing medication adherence and reducing depressive symptoms in this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's non-randomized design may introduce self-selection bias and residual confounding, which could affect the interpretation of the observed associations. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate due to the use of multivariable regression models to adjust for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the impact of a resilience-focused program on depressive symptoms and medication adherence in patients with chronic hepatitis B undergoing antiviral therapy. The study included 200 patients treated at a hepatology clinic between July 2022 and June 2025, with 100 receiving the resilience program and 100 receiving standard care. Primary outcomes included depression scores measured by PHQ-9 and medication adherence by MPR, while secondary outcomes encompassed resilience, virological response, ALT normalization, quality of life, and healthcare utilization. Results showed that the resilience group had lower depression scores, higher MPR, and improved virological and biochemical outcomes. The authors concluded that resilience-based care may enhance treatment outcomes for chronic hepatitis B patients. However, the non-randomized design raises concerns about self-selection bias and residual confounding, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Near-Full-Length Hepatitis B Virus Genomes Isolated from Cerebrospinal Fluid of People Living with HIV and Cryptococcal Meningitis in Botswana

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background/Objectives: Increasing evidence suggests that the hepatitis B virus (HBV) can be detected in extrahepatic compartments. The study aimed to characterize HBV genomes from plasma and CSF and compare paired sequences for genetic similarity and potential compartment-specific differences.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Archived plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from people living with HIV (PLWH) with cryptococcal meningitis (CM) in Botswana enrolled in the AMBITION-CM trial (2018–2021) were used. Four sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences.
analysis.methods: Near-full-length HBV genomes were sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Genotyping and mutational analysis were performed, and paired plasma–CSF sequences were compared to identify genetic differences.
analysis.main_results: The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3. The single plasma–CSF paired sample showed high genetic similarity and had a compartment-specific mutation. Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants (Q ≥ 30) in plasma and CSF, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Clinically relevant mutations were observed in the CSF, warranting further investigation of HBV in the CSF to confirm these observations in PLWH with CM.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the potential for HBV to be present in CSF and suggest the need for further research on HBV in extrahepatic compartments, particularly in PLWH with CM, to better understand its role in disease progression and treatment outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small number of participants, and the evidence is based on a single plasma–CSF pair. The confidence in these findings is moderate due to the limited sample size and the need for further validation in larger studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize hepatitis B virus (HBV) genomes from plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of people living with HIV and cryptococcal meningitis in Botswana. Using Oxford Nanopore Technology, four near-full-length HBV sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences. The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3, and the single plasma–CSF pair showed high genetic similarity with a compartment-specific mutation. Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants in plasma and CSF, respectively. The study found clinically relevant mutations in CSF, such as those associated with hepatocellular carcinoma and antiviral resistance, suggesting the need for further investigation of HBV in CSF. However, the findings are based on a limited number of participants, and the confidence in these results is moderate.

title: The core obstacles and immunological mechanisms in the study of functional cure for Chronic Hepatitis B

analysis.scope_and_question: Attaining a functional cure constitutes the paramount therapeutic objective in the management of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), as it markedly reduces the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma and the progression to terminal liver disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review comprehensively integrates recent progress in understanding the virological mechanisms responsible for HBV persistence, host immune responses to HBV infection, and emerging immunotherapeutic interventions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Major impediments to achieving this outcome include the persistent existence of viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), integration of the viral genome into the host’s DNA, immune tolerance resulting from prolonged exposure to elevated viral antigen levels, and host-mediated HBV-specific immune exhaustion and dysfunction at multiple regulatory levels.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: A thorough elucidation of the molecular pathways underpinning these barriers, alongside their associated immune regulatory networks, is critical for the advancement of novel therapeutic strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The aim is to establish a theoretical foundation and provide critical perspectives to support the clinical translation of approaches designed to achieve a functional cure for CHB.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the challenges and immunological mechanisms involved in achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). It highlights the persistent obstacles such as viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), immune tolerance, and host-mediated immune exhaustion. The review integrates recent findings on virological mechanisms, host immune responses, and immunotherapeutic interventions to provide a theoretical foundation for future clinical applications. It emphasizes the need for a deeper understanding of molecular pathways and immune regulatory networks to develop effective therapeutic strategies. The review also outlines the importance of translating these insights into practical approaches for the treatment of CHB.

title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration

analysis.scope_and_question: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as predictors of extended interferon therapy. It highlights the need to understand these factors as indicators of the virus-host equilibrium rather than just statistical covariates. The authors suggest that high hepatitis B surface antigen levels may signal an established viral reservoir that hampers immune responses, while cirrhosis is viewed as a structural change affecting immune surveillance and therapeutic access. They argue that treatment duration may need to exceed 48 weeks to address these barriers. The review advocates for future predictive modeling to integrate viral kinetics and histological features to improve precision medicine for chronic hepatitis B.

title: Novel HEP-FIB score combined with machine learning models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B patients: a single-center, internally validated study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Assessment of hepatic fibrosis is important for risk stratification and guiding treatment in CHB.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort of 382 CHB patients was analyzed. The study was a single-center, internally validated study. The study focused on chronic hepatitis B patients.
analysis.methods: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of fibrosis. We developed and internally validated HEP-FIB, a parsimonious score based on routinely available laboratory parameters, and evaluated machine learning (ML) models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients.
analysis.main_results: The HEP-FIB score demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, achieving an AUC of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.859–0.925). At the optimal cutoff value (≥ 4), the score showed a sensitivity of 78%, specificity of 89%, and overall accuracy of 88%. The HEP-FIB score outperformed APRI (AUC 0.724), FIB-4 (AUC 0.654), and GPR (AUC 0.773) (all p < 0.001 by DeLong test). Bootstrap validation showed stable performance with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.881. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed fibrosis probabilities, while DCA demonstrated superior net clinical benefit over default strategies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A novel HEP-FIB score was developed based on platelet count, liver function parameters, and lipid biomarkers. Ensemble ML models achieved marginally superior predictive accuracy over HEP-FIB score.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The HEP-FIB score demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for identifying significant hepatic fibrosis in CHB and outperformed conventional non-invasive fibrosis scores in this retrospective, single-center cohort after internal bootstrap validation. The ML models showed a marginal performance advantage over HEP-FIB score.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: External validation in independent and diverse CHB populations is required before the score can be recommended for routine clinical use. The supplied evidence does not report on the generalisability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a non-invasive tool for predicting significant hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B patients. The researchers created the HEP-FIB score using routine laboratory parameters and evaluated machine learning models for predictive performance. The HEP-FIB score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy, with an AUC of 0.892 and a sensitivity of 78% at the optimal cutoff. It outperformed existing non-invasive indices like APRI, FIB-4, and GPR. Additionally, XGBoost, an ensemble ML model, achieved the best predictive performance with an AUC of 0.914. The study found that the ML models showed a marginal advantage over the HEP-FIB score. However, the authors emphasized the need for external validation in diverse populations before recommending the score for routine use. The study's findings suggest that the HEP-FIB score and ML models could improve the non-invasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients, offering better diagnostic and predictive capabilities than traditional methods.

title: Expression of key factors in the TGF-β1/Smad2 pathway and their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma and evaluate their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective single-center cohort study was conducted, enrolling 120 patients with HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma between April 2022 and April 2024.
analysis.methods: TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis were examined using correlation analysis, logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
analysis.main_results: TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was significantly higher in tumor tissue than in paired adjacent non-tumor tissue (both P < 0.001). Higher expression was associated with poorer differentiation and more advanced stage (P < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that elevated expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 in tumors is linked to aggressive clinicopathological features and a poorer prognosis, suggesting their potential as biomarkers for disease progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of targeted therapies and improve prognostic assessment for patients with HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and relatively short follow-up period, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma and their associations with clinicopathological features and prognosis. A prospective single-center cohort of 120 patients was enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024. TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was assessed using immunohistochemistry in paired tumor and non-tumor tissues, and their associations were analyzed with statistical methods. Results showed significantly higher expression of both markers in tumor tissue compared to non-tumor tissue, with higher expression linked to poorer differentiation and more advanced stages. The authors concluded that elevated expression of these markers is associated with aggressive features and worse prognosis, suggesting their potential as biomarkers. The study's findings may contribute to improved prognostic assessment and guide targeted therapeutic strategies. However, the single-center design and limited follow-up period may restrict generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.
